verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a framework for building real-time voice and multimodal agents, so background automation is a fair axis, but the evidence documents no user-configurable automations, schedules or triggers that run autonomously in the background. The closest items are adjacent: in-conversation handoff to subagents for long-running tools, and inbound carrier webhooks or REST calls that start sessions. These are developer building blocks or conversation features, not a background automation capability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
